document_source: England Regulations Approved Document-B Volume 1 Fire Safety with updated 2019 and 2022 Amendments.

regulations.regulation_name: The minimum door width required for the escape route plan
regulations.description: The doorway or the nearest door exit should be open to escape such that it is having 750mm wide and at a minimum of 90 degrees if more than 60 people might be expected to use it during a fire emergency.

regulations.regulation_name: The amount of door opening with minimum direction for possible escape route
regulations.description: All the doors on escape route should be hung and open by a minimum of 90 degrees with a swing clear in case of any change of the floor level.

regulations.regulation_name: Building Storey Height with an escape route
regulations.description: This provides an alternative escape route with two or more storeys that are more than 4.5m above the ground level.

regulations.regulation_name: Construction and design of common stairs
regulations.description: A firefighting stair or a common stair in a building with a storey should have 18m or more in height and be atleast 1100mm wide and any handrails or strings intruding should be maximum 100mm ignoring each side.

regulations.regulation_name: Sill height of emergency escape windows
regulations.description: The bottom of the openable area of an emergency escape window should be a maximum of 1100mm above the floor.
The escape windows should have an unobstructed openable area atleast minimum are of 0.33 square metre.

regulations.regulation_name: The Emergency Escape windows with minimum height and width
regulations.description: The Escape windows should have a minimum height of 450mm and minimum width of 450mm along with the 0.33sqm area.
The Lift wells must be enclosed with a protected stairway and different compartments should form a protected shaft. In basements, the lift should be within the enclosure of a protected stairway.

When any evacuation shaft is provided, it should be located within an evacuation shaft containing a protected stairway, evacuation lift and lobby. The lobby must provide a refuge area for those waiting for the evacuation lift, have direct access to a stair and not be accessible from any flat, storage room or electrical equipment room.
Every floor slab and wall in the building should have the minimum fire resistance upto 60 mins and have the complete barrier between the compartment walls.
Every part of the building must have one final exit giving direct access to a place of safety outside the building.
Every storey should have at least two escape routes so that the occupants have an alternative way out if one route is blocked by another space containing a fire hazard.
